title: CreativeEvent
description: One thing the creative pipeline was asked to do, or one thing it finished — as it travels between the system that asks and the system that works. Commands go one way and results come back the other way over the same relay, so they are one shape with one type field rather than two. The event carries no content: what it carries is an id of something a system already holds, and enough words to act on it. Keys are snake_case, not the camelCase the rest of leaf uses: this travels inside a Liquid envelope, whose own fields (event_id, occurred_at, event_type, owner_unit_ref) are snake_case and pinned byte-exact by signed golden vectors. The shape follows the wire.

id.description: The record's own id in the system that holds it. Also what makes the event replayable without doing the work twice: a reader that has seen this id has already acted.

author.description: ed25519 public key, hex, of whoever signed the event. The only thing that says who asked: a reader admits an event by this key, never by the name below.

author_name.description: What the signing system calls itself, such as creativeflow. A label for reading a log; it proves nothing, and two systems may well claim the same one.

event_type.description: What happened, written as <domain>.<action>. The requested forms are commands addressed to the pipeline; the rest are results it emits. It alone decides which payload shape applies — two different commands can carry the same single id and are told apart by nothing else.

payload.description: What the event is about. Open on purpose: eventType decides which schema the payload is, and a reader picks that type rather than matching on the shape. The union used to live here as anyOf and the generator kept only its first branch, so the other fourteen payloads had no type at all; each is now its own schema. asset.ingest_requested -> AssetIngestRequested; asset.url_ingest_requested -> AssetUrlIngestRequested; generation.requested -> GenerationRequested; repurpose.requested -> RepurposeRequested; rag.query_requested -> RagQueryRequested; asset.edit_requested -> AssetEditRequested; read.completed -> ReadCompleted; derivative.created -> DerivativeCreated; citation.created -> CitationCreated; value.snapshot -> ValueSnapshot; signal.error -> SignalError; generation.ready -> GenerationReady; rag.result_ready -> RagResultReady; repurpose.ready -> RepurposeReady; asset.edit_ready -> AssetEditReady.

content_id.description: The asset, generation or job the event is about, repeated outside the payload so a reader can file the event without opening it. Absent for events about no single thing, such as an error.

owner_unit_ref.description: The session or unit the event belongs to, which is who answers for it. Set on errors above all, where it is the only thing saying whose work broke.

device_id.description: The device the event was written on, when more than one writes for the same author.

lamport.description: A counter for ordering events from one author when wall clocks disagree. Comparable only against events from the same author.

occurred_at.description: When the author says it happened, which is not when a reader received it.
